status_summary: Trade promotion funding has expanded, the opposite of the recommended repeal: Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) contains a section 10602 supplemental agricultural trade promotion program, which CRS reports provides $285 million a year in CCC funding from FY2027, and USDA separately made $285 million available for an America First Trade Promotion Program under the CCC Charter Act, announced on 2025-11-20. USDA opened FY2027 applications for the Market Access Program, the Foreign Market Development Program and other export programs on 2026-06-10, and the FY2027 FAS budget notes propose ending McGovern-Dole and Food for Peace food aid, not MAP or FMD. The House passed H.R. 7567 on 2026-04-30 (224 to 200), which CRS reports would raise mandatory trade promotion funding to $500 million in FY2027 while repealing the supplemental program, and the Senate Agriculture Committee advanced its Agricultural Act of 2026 by 12 to 11 on 2026-09-16, a bill whose June draft was reported to more than double MAP and FMD funding. No proposal to repeal MAP was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was signed; its section 10602 creates a supplemental agricultural trade promotion program, which CRS reports is funded at $285 million a year from FY2027.

USDA announced $285 million in awards funding for the America First Trade Promotion Program for nonprofit trade organizations, state regional trade groups, cooperatives and state agencies, with applications due 2026-01-23; the funding notice cites the CCC Charter Act.

The FY2027 FAS budget notes eliminated McGovern-Dole and Food for Peace funding, listed MAP and FMD among CCC export programs without proposing cuts, and showed a $268.8 million FY2027 line for the supplemental trade promotion program after sequestration.
A CRS primer reported that H.R. 7567 would nearly double mandatory CCC funding for trade promotion programs to $500 million in FY2027 and repeal the reconciliation law's supplemental program.
The House passed H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, by 224 to 200 (roll call 154); the bill was received in the Senate on 2026-05-19.
USDA opened FY2027 applications for the Market Access Program, Foreign Market Development Program and other export development programs.

The Senate Agriculture Committee voted 12 to 11 to advance its farm bill, the Agricultural Act of 2026, whose draft text released in June was reported to more than double Market Access Program and Foreign Market Development Program funding.

title: Focus FAS on trade barriers and repeal export promotion programs such as MAP
uncertainties: The section 10602 heading was confirmed in the enrolled law's table of contents on GovInfo, but the GovInfo page was cut short before the section body, so the $285 million amount and FY2027 start come from the CRS primer. The FY2027 FAS notes show a $285 million transfer, about $16.2 million in sequestration and a $268.8 million appropriation line, which reconciles the two figures. The CRS primer gives MAP and FMD floors of $200 million and $34.5 million a year through FY2026; the FY2027 level was not found. The America First program date of 2025-11-20 is the award-funding announcement shown on the FAS program page; the program was first announced in September 2025 as part of a three-point trade plan, and the funding notice carries no posting date. Whether FAS increased work on sanitary and phytosanitary and other trade barriers (the Mandate's positive recommendation) was not measured. The House farm bill trade provisions come from CRS, not bill text. Related to c10-03 (farm subsidies and CCC). The House vote on H.R. 7567 was read in GovInfo BILLSTATUS (latest action shown: received in the Senate 2026-05-19; record updated 2026-09-25, the final part of the file not read). The Senate committee vote of 12 to 11 on 2026-09-16 comes from news reports (The National News Desk, Drovers), not from the committee's site, and the Senate draft's MAP and FMD increase comes from a Feedstuffs summary that gives no amounts; the Senate bill number and text were not read. Trade press reported the House passing an FY2027 agriculture appropriations bill 213 to 210 in early June 2026; its bill number and its MAP and FAS lines were not found, and no FAS reorganization was found.
